Predict method for weight fits

Source: R/predict.R
predict.kb_fit_weight.Rd

Predict the expected weight at the rows of new_data, or at the observed data when new_data = NULL. Equivalent to kb_predict_weight().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'kb_fit_weight'
predict(
  object,
  new_data = NULL,
  ...,
  new_levels = c("average", "sample"),
  representative_site = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  estimate = stats::median,
  sig_fig = 3
)

Arguments

object

A kb_fit_weight object.

new_data

A data frame of the rows to predict at, with the fit's predictor column (diameter_mm or fronds) and optional site and year columns, or NULL for the observed data. year may be numeric or character: 2022 and "2022" match the same fitted year.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

new_levels

A string giving how uncertainty is estimated for a site or year not in the data used to fit the model, or when new_data has no site or year column. Sites and years in the model fit always use their own estimates. One of:

  • "average" (the default): the typical site or year. The site and year effects are set to 0, their mean, so the interval does not include among-site or among-year variation. Use it to describe an average site or year.

  • "sample": a new effect for each new site or year, drawn from the estimated variation among sites or among years (the random-effect standard deviation). The point estimate is equivalent, but the interval is wider since it also includes that variation. Use it to get realistic uncertainty about a particular site or year that the model has no information on. The interval varies slightly between calls; use set.seed() to reproduce it.

representative_site

A character vector of sites in the fit whose effects a new site adopts (averaged when several are named), or NULL (the default) to follow new_levels.

conf_level

A number greater than 0 and less than 1 giving the compatibility-interval level.

estimate

A function that reduces a numeric vector of posterior draws to a single estimate, such as median or mean.

sig_fig

A whole number of significant figures for summary output.

Value

A kb_predictions object.

See also

Other prediction functions: autoplot.kb_predictions(), kb_new_data(), kb_plot_predictions(), kb_predict_biomass_canopy(), kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(), kb_predict_carbon(), kb_predict_cover_calibration(), kb_predict_mean_weight(), kb_predict_nitrogen(), kb_predict_size(), kb_predict_weight(), kb_predict_wetdry(), predict.kb_fit_carbon(), predict.kb_fit_cover_calibration(), predict.kb_fit_nitrogen(), predict.kb_fit_size(), predict.kb_fit_wetdry()

Examples

predict(fit_weight_sim_nereo, data.frame(diameter_mm = c(20, 40)))
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: diameter_mm | response: weight_kg
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   diameter_mm estimate lower upper
#>         <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1          20    0.434 0.368 0.522
#> 2          40    2.41  1.94  3.08
